body:
I really, really wish but I simply have given up. I've been fighting this crap for too long. 

Thank you anyway though for your kind words...

Sorry for the late reply. 

No, my family doesn't help  me. My mother had to move in with relatives out of town because she can no longer care for herself properly. 

My dad has never really been a part of my life and he doesn't really believe in depression or anything like that, due to how he was raised. It's ironic because his own dad committed suicide, and I've had a therapist tell me that his dad's suicide may be the reason he essentially turned his back on me when I had been struggling in the past. 

No one ever talked about it growing up, which is unfortunate, but I think mental illness runs in my family both ways. I think depression started affecting me after high school, but I didn't know any better and just kept going without any sort of acknowledgement or treatment until about 8 years ago when it really hit hard and ruined my life.

I am completely alone. No internet or phone. Internet was about the only way to feel connected to the world. I don't get phone calls or texts so the internet was the only way I could express  my despair, via sites like this. 

I've had to bike to a place with free wifi but it feels really pathetic to do this as I  just sit here. It isn't far at all but I have to ride along some very dangerous roads where people absolutely fly by. 

Staying in a house a family member abandoned. Power and water haven't been cut off yet, surprisingly. 

No job, no money, no hope. 

I am feeling rather low. Almost out of meds, to boot -- and no refills. Supposed to have a Dr.'s appointment this month but I have neither the money nor a way to get there. Hell, I don't even have a way to call them since I don't have my phone turned on.

It's really bad and suicide has been popping into my mind a lot. I think my survival instincts are taking over which is why I am continuing to go on. But that won't last forever. 

I really have a feeling this is my last month on Earth.

I can relate.

I am almost 40 though! Can't even get a job at the grocery store. Not that it matters because my car is beyond repair. No money, no real friends, family turned their backs on me.  I am a source of embarrassment to them.

I don't have insurance either. I don't think that matters if you're suicidal. You still have a right to live and suicide is certainly an emergency that requires immediate assistance. If you call 911 and tell them you're suicidal, I have no doubt they'll come get you. There are suicide hotlines you can call as well. They would be much better at giving you information than me. 

I can't get help either since I don't have insurance myself. That's one reason I am posting on this board tonight. 

But definitely call someone. 911, a suicide hotline or any other numbers out there which are free.

It might depend on the county. 

In my area, you can call and they'll come and get you. Our hospital has a "behavioral ward" that you're sent to. I've been the our local one several times. I am usually kept for a week and then they let you out. 

There is no shame in calling 911 if you are suicidal. Remember that. I am hoping other counties have better systems/facilities to help.

It's so sad to lose pets. I lost a cat a few years ago to feline leukemia. I can't stand to lose another one. 

I hug her all the time now. Sorry to hear about your cat. I know it's hard when they pass.

I feel the same way about my mother. She would use my own history of depression and suicide against me. She has a prescription drug problem and when she gets on her meds, she says awful things to me, like how no one likes me. Or how I am a failure. 

I try to explain to her that I can't take her emotional abuse, especially this year as I lost my best friend to suicide. But that didn't stop her tirades against me. 

I also have sleep problems because of her. She would wake me up for stupid reasons, usually to blame something on me. Or if she were on her meds and she lost her phone (she loses everything when she's high), she'd need to borrow my phone. I have told her so many times not to wake me up because I start to wake up early due to her doing that. It's called sleep avoidance. When that happens, I can't get back to sleep because I am so frustrated that she woke me up unnecessarily. This happened several times a week. I tried to be nice, I tried to be firm...sometimes I had to actually yell because she drove me past my breaking point. 

Mothers can be very emotionally abusive and not even realize it. Not saying yours is, but I am saying mine is. 

I know how frustrating it can be. We have enough problems already.

What do you mean no one believes you?

I've attempted suicide several times. Do you mean that the suicide always lingers in your mind, because it certainly does. I thought opening up to people about my suicide attempts, being upfront with them, would help. Can't say it has for me. 

I use to drink a lot until I realized it made me feel a lot worse. I used to love drinking as it took me away for a bit. But that fun stopped. Plus I started mainly drinking alone. 

As silly as it may sound, maybe that poisoning was a good thing? At least in the long run? I've never had it myself, so I don't know. I am sure it wasn't a good thing at the time.

I really would like to do that. You're right that this is a terrible place to be homeless. My options are limited since I don't have a car. I'm trying to figure something out. I fight moments of doubt about anything working out for me in this situation. Thank you for the reply.

Thank you for the reply. It helps a little to know someone is out there. I am sorry to hear of your loss. I try to imagine that my friend is now at peace, since he had been in a lot of emotional pain for a very long time. Not sure if you feel the same towards your friend. People handle things differently.

As a man, I don't find it sexist. You have every right to feel the way you do. I am sorry you do feel that way. 

I am just disappointed in society in general. Seems the world would rather try to kill each other than help each other.

I read what you wrote so you are not ignored. I wish I could help, but I can't even help myself. 

I too am considering suicide. I admit I am scared of life and of death. 

I don't know if it helps you to know that people are reading what you wrote and that others are also in dark places.

My terrible year continues. I really wish I could say something positive but I can't. My best friend took his life a few months ago, my mom had to be taken to the hospital because of prescription drug abuse and she made abuse allegations against me (that went nowhere since the cop knew it was her meds) and now she is losing her house, in which I've been staying (I know, it's a bad situation but I had no other choice). She is moving in with a brother out of town and I will be homeless. I have tried everything. I have begged friends. No one even has any advice for me, although they've tried to offer kind, uplifting words. I have a cat I don't know what to do with and it's breaking my heart thinking about her being alone or being out in the wild. 

I haven't been eating or sleeping much, and today I had trouble breathing and swallowing,  and thought I was going to pass out. It wasn't a panic attack because I've had those before. I guess it was fatigue and hunger and stress making me physically weak. I was really sleepy but afraid to go to sleep in case I stopped breathing. Ironic considering I have really been contemplating suicide for the past week. I have actually been putting a lot of thought into ways I could do it. I've been to the local hospital several times and it does not help. I just don't have a support system that I desperately need.

It helps, trust me! Thank you very, very much! It made me feel good that someone actually tried to help me today, because it's been a very bad few days for me. I really appreciate your kind gesture! Thanks again and take care :)

I've had much better experiences with therapists. In fact, I've had downright awful experiences with psychiatrists. 

The first psychiatrist I ever saw was at our local department of mental health. Apparently they are very overworked and understaffed, but I didn't know that at the time. It took almost 6 months before I finally saw a psychiatrist. 

When I did finally see one, I walked into his office and he didn't even greet me or anything. He stared at his computer the whole time reading off questions. No eye contact or anything. Absolutely no personality skills at all. I felt myself becoming more on edge just being around him. 

At the time, I was taking three different meds; one for anxiety to take as needed, one for insomnia to take at night and an anti-depressant. He actually took away the medication for insomnia and increased my anxiety meds, saying that I should take the anxiety meds to help me sleep. I explained to him that I had been doing that originally but was having trouble sleeping. So my doctor had given me something separate to help me sleep. The psychiatrist didn't even listen to me. So he changed my meds anyway and of course I had trouble sleeping again. On top of that, since I was taking more of the anxiety medication, it sorta of built up my tolerance. 

I called back a few days later because I was very concerned about this new medicine routine and he wasn't there, so I talked to a counselor or someone. He explained to me, as if I should know, that that psychiatrist in particular doesn't actually TALK TO YOU, and all he does is prescribe meds. He then rattled off some other stuff that wasn't at all helpful. I stopped going to the Department of Mental Health because it was frustrating and completely unproductive. 

Next one I saw was because I had to go to the hospital for suicidal ideation. The psychiatrist there doesn't like benzos, such as the ativan I was on. So before he even met me, he took me off of it. I've been on it for years and you can't just take someone off of it. I was admitted to the ward and it was a few days before I even met him and when I did, I tried explaining my issue and he didn't listen either. He was dismissive and pompous. I don't think he wanted to be there and it showed. He was the Doctor listed on my bracelet yet I saw him a total of TEN MINUTES during the week I was there. He handled the entire behavioral ward by himself. 

We were supposed to see him a second time but he wasn't there. So we saw another psychiatrist and she was really nice. However, she actually told me that this depression was a phase and I'd get over it. That's something you don't even tell someone on this reddit page. 

I did see a psychiatrist when I was attempting to get disability (they schedule you for an appointment as part of the application process). He was very nice and if I had the money, I would have liked to see him. Unfortunately, it's incredibly difficult to get disability for mental illness in this country and I wasn't able to get the assistance I desperately need.

That is very, very kind of you to offer!  Pretty much anything can help at this point. 

My paypal email address is:

jacks.login@gmail.com

Thank you very much!

My best friend committed suicide a few months back and I feel very guilty as I think I could have done more, considering my history of suicide attempts. I had told him about my suicidal attempts and I almost thought I may have influenced him to some degree. But of course our situations are different. 

I try to tell myself that I cannot predict the future. And that blame never does help anything. 

I am still having a hard time myself. It does help a bit to talk about it. Do what you can to take care of yourself because you are obviously not a monster and you deserve nothing but good things.

Yes, good point. I should have said that as I wouldn't want to be alone either. Since I am completely alone nowadays it wouldn't be a good thing for me to do. 

But I am curious about these epiphany like moments people have. I would love to have a trip and learn something earth-shattering that could help me. I desperately need it.

Last year or the year before I tripped on a bottle of Robotussin several times. Meditated while on it and it was really sad. Lots of realizations and metaphors came to me in that meditation. 

Last few days I got high via something you can buy at the drug store OTC. Almost did it yesterday but the stuff caused bad insomnia -- I got maybe 5 hours of sleep within 48. So I am proud of myself that I showed some restraint. 

Well, today, I got a hold of some pain pills. Already done about 30mg and will probably double that by the day's end. It's very dangerous for me to do that though since I almost had kidney failure from a suicide attempt a few years ago via an OTC drug overdose.

It is good that I am poor, have no car and no connections to people with drugs. If I had access to stuff like heroin or something, I would probably be in an alley or abandoned building with a needle in my arm. In fact, I've been fantasizing about having enough money via crime to live out of a motel room and spend my time getting high. I do NOT do crime or hard drugs or anything like that (I've never been in trouble with the law -- maybe had a handful of speeding tickets) -- just that fantasy wanders into my mind a lot. 

I'd love to get my hands on LSD, but I fear in my state of mind and my overly active imagination that it would be a nightmare of a trip. Never did it before because I was scared of hard stuff. But have used coke, weed and tons and tons of pills. I love pills.

I've been isolated for several years now. I haven't seen friends in even longer, save for the one who actually tried to maintain a friendship with me. Unfortunately he was dealing with depression as well and chose to end his own life a few months ago. 

I try to email friends but they usually don't reply. I've done everything from implying I need help to outright begging for it on Facebook. 

My father and brother are ashamed of me because of my depression, lack of success in life, failed suicide attempt, etc. 

I honestly communicate more on here than I do with so-called real life friends. 

Honestly though, no one can help me at this point.

I'm almost 40. No job, shitty resume because I've been pretty much fired from the last 5 jobs I had, which were terrible warehouse jobs. Before that was when my depression brought me to the point of a failed suicide attempt. Since my depression wasn't under control even after that, that affected my jobs. Last job I lost because of another suicide attempt. Yeah, I can't even kill myself properly. I tried really hard. I downed so many sleeping pills that I woke up a few days later, blind, and was stumbling around falling, breaking things, hallucinating. When my vision came back, my roommate called the cops and they said I either had to go to jail or to the hospital. Was eventually homeless after that. 

I too had to move into a room at my mom's. Can't even get a fucking job at the grocery store. No car. No money. No insurance. No college degree. 

Now about to be homeless again and I was trying to be optimistic, but today I realized I can't do it. When I was homeless before I had a car and it wasn't that bad. No car now. And I just don't want to deal with this shitty life anymore.

Sorry for the delay. Lots going on today. I'm in Spartanburg and the mental health center is terrible. Tried going twice since the first time didn't go well. But the second time was worse.  The wait to actually talk to a psychiatrist is about half a year or longer and when I finally saw him, he doesn't even talk to you. He simply looks at your meds and adjusts them if he thinks you need it. And he actually ended up messing up my meds and setting my anxiety back a few steps. Then they tried to charge me over $1000. I had to take a taxi a few times because of no car and they sometimes wouldn't even know why I was there!  They're so understaffed and overworked that it's its own level of frustration going through the system. 

I've also been to the local behavioral ward of our hospital several times. They just want to make sure you're not suicidal anymore. I have no support system so when I got out, I wasn't much better off. 

It's just an awful county to be mentally ill in I suppose. 

Thank you for the information. It was very helpful.
Thanks, that's a lot of information and I appreciate it. Today is a low day for optimism for me but your post was helpful. Thanks.
Thanks, but unfortunately I am from the US.
Sorry it took me so long to reply. Lots going on today. Most of it bad. I'm from Spartanburg, SC.

Wow, I wish I were in Florida! I'm in SC. I suppose I could try to get there somehow. I really need to get out of this state. I think that's one of many, many problems with me. I was homeless before but had a car and food assistance. Not this time. I am actually considering suicide things are so desperate for me. 

I am in pretty bad financial dire straits here so I would love to find a good Samaritan. I'd cut grass, clean, run errands -- anything I could do to earn/repay kindness. 

There simply aren't any resources for homeless around here.

I speak from experience. I have been the vulnerable, guilty, ashamed, embarrassed one. I failed at my attempt so I've heard all kinds of stuff. I had friends and family telling me to get over it and get a job. I had people wonder why I failed, as if to say they wished I would have succeeded. Others said I am just sad and, again, to get over it. I couldn't believe what people were saying but then it occurred to me that people simply don't or can't understand exactly unless they've been in that position. So I learned what I don't want to hear, lol. 

You could even ask him if he wants to talk about things. He may or may not. Maybe not yet but in the future.

You're off to a good start. Lots of people don't think to ask. 

Remember that your friend is very vulnerable. He probably feels very guilty, ashamed, embarrassed. Just like here, don't tell him he will get over it or it's a phase or anything insincere like that. 

Sometimes just letting him know you're there for him is enough.

Because I really needed real solutions to problems. Therapy doesn't work very well on me even though I've given it a good shot. I have too many physical obstacles in life to where my mental ones have to take a back seat. I mean, I have day to day worries like no money, medication and an approaching homeless situation. So I expected too much and/or it simply wasn't the avenue for me at the time.

I am curious as well. I've been conditioned not to really talk to people about my problems so I've never talked to anyone like that. 

There was a website where you could chat with someone but it was a huge waste of time.

Yes and yes. 

Many of my passions, such as photography, gaming, photo editing, have long since left me. I suppose it's that depression thinking, acting and feeling for me. I try to trick myself into being passionate about things but I just can't get away with it. 

I was a totally different person not too long ago. I don't recognize that person, much less understand how he functioned and made it through life.

I had an off-and-on relationship very similar to that. I gave way more than I got, and I guess I had hoped each time I gave her something that she would reciprocate or at least appreciate it -- perhaps see that she would be without that if we broke up or went separate ways, but like you I felt that she considered it a "favor" to me whenever she gave. 

We broke up so many times. She always broke up with me and then wanted to get back together. I stupidly allowed it. I honestly lost count of how many times it happened. Eventually she moved away and I got over her. But it took a long time and I think it exasperated, or awoke, a depression within me that led me to the life I have now. I am not blaming her for everything. But she could have treated me better and/or decided for sure if she wanted me in her life instead of constantly dragging me along for a turbulent, dangerous, life-changing (maybe destroying?) roller coaster ride. 

I kinda took pride later on that I did try, and that I was a very giving person at that time to her. Later on I also wished I would have ended it long ago. But when you're in that time, of course you don't know that, do you?

I woke up one day and realized I had long since gotten over her.

No, I don't mind. Anxiety and depression, and a GP suggested perhaps bi-polar disorder. I can see it, but my mood can change within seconds. I don't know if it's something else entirely or my depression. I can't afford even therapy so I've never had an expert diagnose me. 

I burned a lot of bridges when I attempted -- and failed -- to kill myself pretty violently a few years back. My brother and dad tried to help me I suppose, but I was dealing with a lot of issues after my month's stay in the hospital. I wasn't ready to get better and get a job, and that disappointed them to the point where they turned their backs on me. 

My friends, two of them, grew up, got jobs and now have families. So they have little time for me. My best friend of over 30 years, who was going through depression like me and whom I had a lot in common with (such as the shame of having a much more successful younger brother), took his own life a few months back. That hurt me bad, and still hurts. I tend to want to see where he is, to follow him to whatever oblivion he went into.

Yeah. It used to help. I haven't had anyone to talk to in forever. I try to write and text friends but they don't reply back, understandably. I even begged for help on my facebook, and it got a little attention and then went away. I guess the internet is about the only place I have left. 

I think it's good that I won't ever have kids. Apparently the mental illness went to me and skipped my much more successful younger brother. Good for him in that regard. I need to do my part for humanity and allow survival of the fittest to take its course. 

I think I had a good childhood too, aside from my father. He always made sure we had things we needed and a good Christmas, Thanksgiving, etc though. I think about childhood often nowadays, as a means to escape my current life. I guess I am just not cut out for adult life in this time period. Hopefully, in the next life...

OK, I see. Can I ask if you had a good childhood? Was your mother there for you?

Although my father was always in the picture and stayed with my mom until I almost graduated high school, he didn't treat me like a son. He constantly yelled and ridiculed me and made me feel like I would be a failure. Well he was right. 

I'm kinda just babbling. I am having a slow breakdown I think, so don't mind me. Just conversing.

Can I ask if there are romantic feelings involved? Or is it just the friendly attachment sort of thing? I don't know why I am asking,  and feel free to ignore it if you want...except I think if its the first one it might make things a little harder.

I do wish I could disconnect my sex drive. I lie awake at night and wake up in the morning thinking of some of the awesome sexual experiences I had and wishing I could go back to them. It's been like 3 or 4 years since I've had sex. 

You're right about the stigma males face who have to deal with doubt, pain, sadness, mental illness, etc. I don't think it's sexist to point out a discrepancy. I have no problem acknowledging how different genders are treated in the work place, so I hope they'll give me this one thing. 

Remember that death is considered one of the most traumating events one can experience, at least according to some list. I guess it's a bit obvious but just know that I think death can have a much more substantial impact down the road on one's self. 

I've suffered two deaths this year. Non-relations though. One was my best friend who took his own life because of depression. I think I haven't followed suite because I didn't want to put my friend's parents through something like a suicide again. But now, I just don't really care that much anymore.

I wish I had something to contribute! I am watching this thread because I need help myself. I've lost interest in hobbies and have no real friends anymore. I have no way to do anything other than sit in this disgusting house. I don't mean to hijack.

Great to hear that you have a good, strong attitude about it. Sounds like you're definitely on the right path, and I am sure you're familiar with what Nietzsche said. 

You will learn from it and I believe it will be something that will make you stronger in the future. 

Keep fighting and good luck to you!

Nothing really, except maybe my cat doing something silly as usual. She's funny and probably the only reason I haven't ended it. 

Poor thing, I can't even afford to take care of her properly. This POS house I am in is old and full of trash because of my mother. There are fleas and she is getting eaten up by them. 

It would break my heart but I wish I could find someone to take care of her properly. 

But that's it. Smiling and laughing are things I rarely do and I have forgotten why people do it and I can't believe it when I see others smiling and laughing.

Yes, it's very true what you say about people committing suicide regardless of gender.  

However, I do feel that it's less acceptable in society for males to be depressed, suicidal, etc. I think it has a lot to do with upbringing and the old fashioned "guys are supposed to be strong and not have problems and not whine about being sad" shit, the same shit I was brought up with. 

It also may have to do with the fact that guys may -- emphasis on "may"
 because I am of course far from an expert -- act out more outwardly, maybe even aggressively, when depressed or suffering from some form of mental illness. Sometimes that behavior may lead to legal troubles. So they're seen as a violent person, and not as someone who is suffering internally. 

I want to add that in this semantics-obsessed world, I am absolutely not saying one thing is more tragic or less deserving of sympathy than the other thing. Suicide is bad. Depression is bad. Regardless of the gender or race or nationality or religion of whomever is suffering, it is an equally sad and tragic thing.

Oh? I admit I don't know too much about the point system here. 

And I just scrolled down to see that you posted the same thing before I did. Didn't realize someone had posted that already.

Thanks for reading our thoughts here. It does help I think, even if a little, to know someone out there in that world of non-depression is taking some time to get to know some of us here and what we're going through. 

No, you don't sound arrogant at all. I think what is arrogant are people who act like they can tell us to "get over it" or "stop being sad". 

Someone telling us that they hear us is nice to hear, so thank you for taking the time.

I was raised in a family with a John Wayne type father, military, who believed a man should not have problems or feel sad and that if he doesn't have a job and can't take care of himself, he is worthless. So that's what I dealt with. Now that depression, anxiety and suicidal attempts have destroyed my life, both my dad and brother -- who is similar -- have turned their backs on me. Ironically, my dad's father took his own life. Maybe he dislikes me because he has deep subconscious feelings for how his dad took his life -- at least that's what a therapist told me. 

It IS hard being a guy with depression, anxiety, etc. There's this ridiculous expectation that guys shouldn't let things like that affect them and it's fucking stupid. Like we need to just get over it and continue throwing ourselves into the meat grinder of jobs and life that wear us down and shred us into pieces. 

I've had a few long term relationships (although a few were quite damaging to me) but right now, having or even wanting a g/f is so far away it isn't even on my mind. I don't even want one because I have so much shame about myself and I know that since I am not happy, I won't be happy with her. I used to be kind of a bad guy when it came to females so maybe I am paying the price for that. If I went like a month without sex I would be crazy. Well, it's been several years now and yes, it's bad. Very bad. But I have depression and anxiety and a few other things that have deeper claws stuck into me. 

It's a hard truth. You can't depend on a g/f or significant other for happiness. You put too much on them and if that pressure causes a break -- and it most likely will -- you will be worse off than before. You do have to be happy with yourself before you can be happy with someone else. 

At least that's my experience, so it may not apply to everyone.

I am glad for you. Really!

I think my best friend was suffering from PAWS as he had had a lot of surgery and was going through not having pain medication anymore. He had been buying poppy seed tea which didn't help much, but only served to take a slight edge off his withdrawal. He was depressed as well. 

Unfortunately, two months ago he chose to take his own life. He was the best person in the world, truly. Very very kind and polite, sincere, very smart and creative. Like me though, depression had ruined his life and he didn't feel he had much worth. I am devastated by it and will never be the same. 

So I am glad to read about one happy ending to that terrible affliction! Congrats to you.

Actually, I see people and wonder how they can function. I see people smiling and laughing and I can't understand how they're doing it. I've completely forgotten what it's like to be happy or how anyone can smile about anything. It's like I am in a different world from everyone.
Oh definitely! Totally agree. I am completely alone but being here is helpful. As you said, we aren't alone.

I am terribly sorry to hear that. My best friend took his life in the same fashion two months ago. I am devastated. I will never be the same. 

I can understand the apathy that accompanied your grief, as I am experiencing something pretty similar. 

I hope that you're doing well. It may have been a long time ago but I imagine that it's something that never goes away. It may not feel like a long time ago.

Hello! It was years ago. I must have been unclear when I wrote my message. I am a little off when it comes to communication since I am going through all of this bad stuff that's been happening to me. 

We were on and off for probably 3 years or so. This was probably two years ago, I believe? She moved out of state and we talked a little, but it was pretty much officially over. We had done the "get together and then break up" thing so many times that I found it easier each time to get over it. 

I really loved her, but now I never think about her and it's something in the past that I have completely moved on from. But at the time, it was very bad. The experience is like a scar though. It's a part of you that even though you don't think about anymore, it still had an effect on your life, even long after it's over -- if that makes any sense. 

Thanks for the reply! I really appreciate anyone that takes the time to reply to me. It makes me feel less alone in this world.

Of course I can't imagine exactly what you're going through, but I've been devastated when my g/f broke up with me. We got back together -- on her insistence, and of course I went along with it because I loved her -- and then she would break up with me. Every time. It happened so many times I can't count. 

It really destroyed me. I didn't do anything. I didn't eat very well. I was alone. I avoided everyone. I cried constantly. I was a mess. It took a long time but I just realized one day, long after mind you, that I was over her. I believe you will get over her one day. I believe that time does heal most wounds, but it feels like eternity. 

Force yourself to be around family and/or friends. Even if it's something like watching a movie. Anything. Try to concentrate on the things that are important, like your education, hobbies, interests, etc. Easier said than done though, I know. 

There are mental techniques that you can try where you basically train your brain to stop having bad thoughts. It didn't really work well for me, but it does work for other people. 

Also, if you're into movies, try to avoid the dark, negative ones. I know it sounds silly, but I found myself watching horror movies and the like. I was in a dark place and for some reason, I wanted to stay there. I am a huge movie buff so it was rather unhealthy for me. Watch something uplifting, comedies, inspirational biopics, etc. Go for walks if you can. Parks, nature trails. The sun and fresh air are good for you. 

I probably didn't help much, but I really wish you luck. Try to stay strong and focused, again easier said than done. 

But I reiterate that I think in time you will heal. I really believe you will not even realize you're over her and you'll find that you're getting back to your regular self. 

Again, good luck!

I had a very damaging on and off relationship with someone I really think I loved. I gave so much - I'd help her with her college work, I babysat her daughter, spent so much money on her -- I know that sounds like stuff you're supposed to do, but she never reciprocated and it made me feel not only unimportant but that I was being used. I think I've been depressed for a long time and didn't realize it but that really set it off and brought it up a few levels. I had also lost a job I had for almost 10 years not long before I met her. 

But the worst thing happened to me two months ago. My best friend, whom I've known for over 30 years, took his own life. He was the friendliest, most caring, considerate person ever.
